headline: Nike Founder Pledges $1 Billion to Public University's New Engineering College
meta_description: Phil Knight and his wife Penny donate $1 billion to University of Oregon, enabling the creation of a new engineering college in a state facing engineer shortag…
summary_short: Nike founder Phil Knight has made history with a $1 billion donation to the University of Oregon—the largest single gift ever given to an American public university.
body:
Nike founder Phil Knight and his wife Penny have made a transformative gift to the University of Oregon: $1 billion toward the creation of an entirely new engineering college. University President Karl Scholz received the unexpected call in September while sitting in a San Francisco airport terminal, a moment that evidently caught even the institution's leadership off guard. The Times reports this is the largest single donation to an American public university in history—a distinction that underscores both Knight's extraordinary generosity and his confidence in higher education's future. For Oregon, the gift solves a long-standing puzzle: how to consolidate various engineering programs into a cohesive, full-fledged undergraduate program at a time when Oregon faces a documented shortage of engineers.

Knight's relationship with the university runs remarkably deep. His name already graces the law center, sports complexes, and library across campus, and his foundation has previously donated $1 billion in combined gifts over the decades—a history that led some to informally call it the University of Nike. Yet this single commitment dwarfs those earlier contributions and arrives at a critical moment. Vice President Bob Guldberg and Scholz had kept Knight informed of their engineering ambitions for years, but neither expected such decisive action. In his statement, Knight emphasized that realizing such dreams requires more than imagination—it demands the kind of institutional opportunity that America's universities have historically provided.

The donation arrives as the university anticipated budget pressures ahead. The gift not only transforms the engineering program but signals a powerful vote of confidence in public higher education itself, just when such institutional support matters most.
